llm.summary: This Kia Access skill is mostly coherent, but it asks users to place vehicle-account credentials in MCP config and creates long-lived local session access for sensitive vehicle location and commands.

dimensions.detail: Network access to Kia and account credentials are expected for the purpose, and the artifact cautions against echoing secrets, guessing vehicle keys, or retrying failed logins.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses npx to run kiaaccess-mcp and shows KIA_USERNAME and KIA_PASSWORD stored directly in project or global MCP configuration, which is sensitive for an account that can expose vehicle location and remote commands.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill documents write-mode scoping and confirm-gated commands, including dry-run behavior and warnings for unlocking, but the default example enables comfort commands rather than read-only mode.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact discloses a local remember-me token that refreshes sessions silently indefinitely and a plaintext refresh-token export tool described as a full MFA bypass, which is high-impact even though it is confirm-gated and purpose-aligned.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the documented capabilities: reading Kia vehicle status, charge state, location, and issuing user-confirmed climate, charging, lock, and unlock commands through the user's Kia account.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving this MCP server access to your Kia account. Prefer read-only KIA_WRITE_MODE=none unless you need remote commands, avoid storing the password or refresh token in shared project config, protect any local MCP config and backups, and use kia_forget_session if the machine or account access should no longer be trusted.
llm.findings: [AS2] expected: Kia credentials are expected for this integration, but the artifact-backed concern is valid because the setup example places the password in MCP config and the same account can enable vehicle location access and remote commands.
